title_en: Song Peng v. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Nanjing Xinmenkou Sub-branch — dispute over debit card
ruling_gist_en: 1. Banks have the obligation to ensure the safety of depositors' deposits, and should strive to improve and enhance the anti-counterfeiting technology of bank cards to the greatest extent to prevent depositors' bank cards from being stolen and fraudulently used.
keywords_en: Civil; Debit card dispute; First instance; Basic people's court; Jiangsu Province; Henan Province; Natural person; Financial institution; Contract Law; Determination of counterfeit card transaction; Effectiveness of clause treating password as transaction by the cardholder; Bank's duty of security and safety; Allocation of burden of proof; Supporting plaintiff; Fraudulent use of debit card; Remote withdrawal; Reporting to police and reporting loss; Good faith; Debit card dispute of Nanjing Xinmenkou Sub-branch
full_text_en:
Song Peng v. China Industrial and Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Nanjing Xinmenkou Sub-branch — dispute over debit card

【Ruling Summary】

I. A bank bears the obligation to ensure the safety of depositors' funds and shall endeavor to improve and upgrade the anti-counterfeiting technology of bank cards to the maximum extent to prevent depositors' bank cards from being skimmed or counterfeited.

II. The provision in the debit card bylaws that "all transactions made using a password are deemed by the issuing bank to have been performed by the cardholder personally" applies only to genuine debit card transactions and does not apply to transactions made with counterfeit cards; the bank cannot be exempted from liability on this basis.

III. In the absence of any evidence that the cardholder personally disclosed the bank card password, the cardholder shall not be ordered to bear partial losses, thereby reducing the bank's liability for compensation.

Plaintiff: Song Peng, male, 22 years old, of Han ethnicity, residing in Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: China Industrial and Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Nanjing Xinmenkou Sub-branch, domiciled at Xinmenkou, Gulou District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Person in charge: Lan Lina, Branch Manager.

The plaintiff, Song Peng, brought an action against the defendant, China Industrial and Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Nanjing Xinmenkou Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch), concerning a dispute over a debit card, to the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Plaintiff's Allegations: At approximately 2:00 a.m. on August 5, 2015, his salary card issued by ICBC was used for six withdrawals at an ATM, totaling RMB 14,000, along with handling fees of RMB 94. At around 6:00 a.m. that day, after seeing the SMS notifications on his mobile phone, he immediately called ICBC's 95588 hotline, reported the card lost, and filed a police report. Subsequent inquiries with the bank revealed that the withdrawals occurred at a rural credit cooperative ATM in a township of Zhumadian City, Henan Province. Song Peng argued that the bank has an obligation to ensure the safety of the funds in his account. His bank card had never left his possession and was in normal use; he himself had not performed any withdrawals or transfers on August 5, 2015. Therefore, the bank had breached the contract and should be liable for compensation for his losses. He requested that the defendant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch be ordered to compensate him for the loss of RMB 14,094 and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant's Defense: When the plaintiff Song Peng applied to open the account, both parties agreed that transactions made using the password would be deemed as transactions by the cardholder himself. The funds in question were withdrawn using the correct password, and the bank had fulfilled its payment obligation. After the transaction in question occurred, Song Peng had sufficient time to travel between Zhumadian and Nanjing. The existing evidence is insufficient to prove that the bank card was used fraudulently with a counterfeit card. The public security authorities have already initiated a criminal investigation into this case. Pursuant to law, Song Peng's lawsuit should be dismissed, and the case should be transferred to the public security authorities for handling, or the proceedings should be suspended pending the criminal investigation. Even if fraud involving a counterfeit card occurred, it is obvious that Song Peng disclosed his password information, and he should bear responsibility for failing to keep the password properly. The rural credit cooperative that processed the bank card transaction was the entity that failed to fulfill its obligation to identify the counterfeit card, if any. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch has no management authority or duty over external institutions and equipment and is not at fault. In summary, the defendant requested that Song Peng's claims be dismissed.

Facts Found by the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing City at First Instance:

On June 19, 2012, the plaintiff Song Peng applied for and obtained a debit card (Peony Lingtong Card) with the number 6222 XXXX XXXX XXXX 828 from the defendant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch. Article 7 of the *Bylaws of China Industrial and Commercial Bank Debit Cards* provides: "To apply for a debit card, a password must be set. The cardholder must use the password to conduct consumption settlements, withdrawals, transfers, and remittances with the debit card (except for chip card electronic cash). All transactions made using the password are deemed by the issuing bank to be performed by the cardholder personally. The electronic information records generated from various transactions processed based on the password and other electronic information shall be valid evidence of such transactions. The cardholder shall properly keep the debit card and password. The issuing bank shall not be liable for losses caused by the cardholder's failure to keep them properly. ..." This provision is printed in small font, identical in appearance to the other provisions, with no obvious distinction.

At around 2:00 a.m. on August 5, 2015, the funds in Song Peng's said account were withdrawn six times from a rural credit cooperative ATM in Zhumadian City, Henan Province, totaling RMB 14,094 (including handling fees of RMB 94). According to the SMS records received by Song Peng, the withdrawal times and amounts were as follows: 02:18, RMB 2,500, fee RMB 16.50; 02:18, RMB 2,500, fee RMB 16.50; 02:19, RMB 2,500, fee RMB 16.50; 02:19, RMB 2,500, fee RMB 16.50; 02:20, RMB 2,500, fee RMB 16.50; 02:20, RMB 1,500, fee RMB 11.50.

At 9:54 a.m. on August 5, 2015, the plaintiff Song Peng, because his bank card had been swallowed, went through the procedures for retrieving the swallowed card at ICBC. At 9:57 a.m. that day, Song Peng reported the matter to the Zhongyangmen Police Station of the Gulou Sub-bureau of the Nanjing Public Security Bureau, stating that RMB 14,000 had been fraudulently withdrawn from his ICBC salary card. At approximately 10:09 a.m. that day, police officers from the Zhongyangmen Police Station took an interview record from Song Peng. At the same time, the police station issued a case filing decision [2015] No. 9226 (Gu Gong (Yang) Li Zi), initiating a criminal investigation into the theft of the RMB in Song Peng's bank card.

It was also found that the plaintiff Song Peng was a soldier of the People's Liberation Army Unit 94991. During the trial, the unit issued a certificate to the court, the main content of which stated that Song Peng had been at his unit at No. 1 Zhongfu Road, Nanjing, from 2:18 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. on August 5, 2015, and had never left.

The plaintiff Song Peng described the incident as follows: On the morning of August 5, 2015, after seeing the SMS notifications on his phone, he immediately reported it to his unit leaders and called the ICBC customer service hotline to report the card lost. The customer service representative informed him that the withdrawals had taken place in Zhumadian City, Henan Province, and told him to go through the relevant procedures after the bank opened. Subsequently, when he went to handle the loss reporting procedures, because he had already reported the loss by phone, the card was swallowed, so he went through the card retrieval procedures. After completing the procedures at the bank, he also reported the matter to the Zhongyangmen Police Station.

During the trial, the defendant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch did not submit any evidence to prove that Song Peng had disclosed his password or authorized others to use his bank card, nor did it submit any evidence to prove that Song Peng had traveled between Zhumadian and Nanjing on August 5, 2015.

Opinion of the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing City at First Instance:

The plaintiff Song Peng holds a debit card issued by the defendant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch. A savings deposit contract relationship was lawfully established between him and ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch. As a professional financial institution engaged in deposit and lending business, ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch bears the obligation to ensure the safety of depositors' funds. In this case, Song Peng's debit card was used for six withdrawals totaling RMB 14,094 (including handling fees) at a rural credit cooperative ATM in Zhumadian City, Henan Province, at around 2:00 a.m. on August 5, 2015. After discovering the SMS notifications regarding these withdrawals, Song Peng called the ICBC customer service hotline to report the loss, subsequently went through the relevant procedures at the bank, and reported the matter to the Zhongyangmen Police Station. According to the certificate issued by the People's Liberation Army Unit 94991, Song Peng did not leave his unit during the time period when the remote withdrawals occurred on his bank card. Considering all the existing facts, it is sufficient to determine that Song Peng was in possession of the debit card and was present in Nanjing at the time of the six aforementioned withdrawals. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch argued that the six withdrawals could not be definitively identified as fraudulent transactions using a counterfeit card. However, since the bank holds the majority of evidence regarding the debit card transaction process, the burden of proof should be on the bank to demonstrate that the deposits were withdrawn lawfully and properly. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch failed to prove that the debit card in question was used for lawful and proper withdrawals, that Song Peng had traveled between Zhumadian and Nanjing at the time of the bank card transactions, or that Song Peng had authorized others to use the debit card or disclosed his password. Therefore, it must bear the legal consequences of its failure to meet its burden of proof. In summary, Song Peng's claim that the deposits in his debit card account were fraudulently withdrawn by someone else at a remote location is accepted by the court. The debit card in question is a UnionPay card. The transaction processed by a rural credit cooperative in Zhumadian, Henan, using a counterfeit card was performed on behalf of ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch. Therefore, it is determined that ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch failed to fulfill its duty of prevention regarding the anti-counterfeiting technology of the debit card in question, constituting a breach of contract. Song Peng's claim for compensation of RMB 14,094 in deposit losses has factual and legal basis and is supported. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch's argument that Song Peng should assert his rights against the rural credit cooperative has no legal basis and is not accepted.

Regarding the issue that transactions made using a password are deemed to be made by the cardholder himself: The *Bylaws of China Industrial and Commercial Bank Debit Cards* provide that "all transactions made using a password are deemed by the issuing bank to be performed by the cardholder personally." This clause is a standard form clause unilaterally drafted by the bank, which has the effect of exempting its own liability, increasing the other party's liability, and excluding the other party's primary rights. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch was obligated by law to bring this clause to Song Peng's attention and clearly explain it. Since this clause is not visually distinct from other clauses, is printed in small font, and the existing evidence cannot prove that the defendant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch lawfully brought the content of this clause to the plaintiff Song Peng's attention and clearly explained it, this clause is null and void and shall not apply.

Regarding whether this case should be transferred to the public security authorities: The plaintiff Song Peng initiated this lawsuit based on the savings deposit contract relationship between him and the defendant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch. The civil liability that ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch bears under the savings deposit contract is not the same legal relationship as the criminal liability that others bear for using bank cards to commit fraudulent withdrawals. Pursuant to Article 121 of the Contract Law, whether the public security authorities solve this criminal case does not affect Song Peng's right to seek civil liability from the bank through civil proceedings. After ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch assumes liability, it may seek recourse from the responsible parties in accordance with the law. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch's argument that this case should be transferred to the public security authorities or suspended is untenable and is not accepted.

Accordingly, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing City, pursuant to Articles 39, 40, 107, and 121 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 6 and 33 of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 39(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, rendered judgment on November 19, 2015:

The defendant, ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch, shall compensate the plaintiff, Song Peng, for his loss of RMB 14,094.

ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch was dissatisfied and appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court: 1. The first instance judgment's finding that the disputed transaction involved a counterfeit card lacked factual basis. The certificate provided by Song Peng could not prove that his bank card was with him at the time of the transaction. After the transaction in question occurred, Song Peng had sufficient time to travel between Zhumadian and Nanjing. The existing evidence is insufficient to prove that the bank card was used fraudulently with a counterfeit card. The determination of a counterfeit card transaction falls within the realm of criminal adjudication and requires proof beyond a reasonable doubt. 2. The public security authorities have already initiated a criminal investigation into this case. Pursuant to law, Song Peng's lawsuit should be dismissed, and the case should be transferred to the public security authorities or suspended. 3. Even if a counterfeit card transaction was involved, the first instance judgment's finding that the bank bears full liability has no legal basis. When Song Peng applied to open the account, both parties agreed that transactions made using the password would be deemed as transactions by the cardholder himself. The funds in question were withdrawn using the correct password. If a counterfeit card transaction was involved, it is obvious that Song Peng disclosed the card he held and the password he set. In the absence of evidence proving that the bank caused his password to be disclosed, Song Peng should bear corresponding responsibility. The first instance court ignored the cardholder's strict and prudent duty of care regarding the card and especially the password set by himself, and found that the bank bears full liability, which lacks factual basis.

The respondent Song Peng argued in defense: The first instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. He requested that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance during the second instance trial.

Opinion of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court at Second Instance:

The issues of dispute in the second instance were: 1. Whether the disputed transaction constituted a counterfeit card transaction; 2. Whether the case should be dismissed or suspended; 3. The allocation of liability for the deposit loss of the respondent Song Peng.

As to Issue 1, whether the disputed transaction constituted a counterfeit card transaction: Article 108(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that if the evidence provided by the party bearing the burden of proof, upon examination by the people's court and in conjunction with the relevant facts, makes it highly probable that the fact to be proved exists, the people's court shall find that fact to exist. In this case, the respondent Song Peng is a soldier of the People's Liberation Army Unit 94991. His debit card was used for six withdrawals totaling RMB 14,094 (including handling fees) at a rural credit cooperative ATM in Zhumadian City, Henan Province, at approximately 2:00 a.m. on August 5, 2015. After discovering the SMS notifications regarding these withdrawals, Song Peng called the ICBC customer service hotline to report the loss on the morning of the same day. At 9:54 a.m. that day, because his bank card had been swallowed, Song Peng went through the procedures for retrieving the swallowed card at ICBC and reported the matter to the Zhongyangmen Police Station. The certificate issued by the People's Liberation Army Unit 94991 indicates that Song Peng was at his unit at No. 1 Zhongfu Road, Nanjing, from 2:18 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. on August 5, 2015, and had never left. The first instance court, based on these facts and considering factors such as the remote transaction at an unusual hour shortly after midnight, the distance between Zhumadian City, Henan Province, and Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, Song Peng's occupation, the time of his loss reporting and police report, and his statements, did not err in finding that the disputed transaction was a counterfeit card transaction. The appellant's argument that the standard of proof for determining a counterfeit card transaction should be beyond a reasonable doubt has no legal basis and is not supported.

As to Issue 2, whether the case should be dismissed or suspended: The respondent Song Peng's lawsuit is based on the civil savings deposit contract relationship, which is not the same legal relationship as the criminal liability of others for using bank cards to commit fraudulent withdrawals. The savings deposit contract dispute between Song Peng and the appellant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch does not itself involve a crime, nor is there evidence that Song Peng was a co-perpetrator of the fraudulent withdrawals. Therefore, the investigation by the public security authorities does not affect ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch's liability to Song Peng. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Disputes Involving Criminal Suspects, which states that "when a people's court discovers clues or materials concerning an economic crime suspect that are connected to the case but are not the same legal relationship during the trial of an economic dispute case, it shall transfer the clues or materials to the relevant public security or procuratorial authorities for investigation, and the economic dispute case shall continue to be tried," this case shall continue to be tried.

As to Issue 3, the allocation of liability for the deposit loss of the respondent Song Peng: Articles 6 and 33 of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China provide that commercial banks have an obligation to ensure the safety of depositors' deposits. The appellant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch, by providing debit card services to Song Peng, should ensure that the data and information on the debit card cannot be unlawfully obtained and used. Moreover, ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch, as the issuing bank and the provider of the relevant technology, equipment, and operating platform, occupies a clearly dominant position in the contractual relationship with the depositor and should bear the obligation to identify counterfeit cards. The fact that the counterfeit card transaction could be carried out indicates that the data information on Song Peng's genuine bank card could be copied and stored onto another counterfeit card, and the counterfeit card could still conduct normal transactions after inputting the password. Therefore, the debit card issued by ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch and its transaction system had defects in anti-counterfeiting technology. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch failed to fulfill its obligation to ensure transaction safety, causing economic losses to Song Peng, and should bear liability for compensation. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch appealed, arguing that Song Peng was at fault for disclosing the transaction password, but it did not provide any evidence to prove that Song Peng failed to properly keep and reasonably use the debit card he held. It must bear the legal consequences of its failure to meet its burden of proof. Although the ICBC debit card bylaws provide that all transactions made using a password are deemed by the issuing bank to be performed by the cardholder personally, the application of this rule is premised on the party conducting the transaction using a genuine debit card. Therefore, ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch, in the absence of evidence proving that Song Peng was in breach of contract or engaged in any criminal or unlawful conduct, shall bear the initial liability for the loss of funds. ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch's claim that Song Peng should bear corresponding responsibility in the absence of proof that the bank caused his password to be disclosed is not supported.

In summary, the appeal requests and grounds of the appellant ICBC Xinmenkou Sub-branch lack factual and legal basis and shall not be supported. The first instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and the judgment shall be affirmed.

Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered judgment on February 23, 2016:

Appeal dismissed; judgment affirmed.

This judgment is final.
